title: Don't Be Shy trailer drops: Alia Bhatt's coming-of-age rom-com bets on fresh faces
excerpt: The first trailer for Prime Video's Don't Be Shy introduces four debutant leads headed by Aarushi Bajaj, as producers Alia Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt back a young-adult story of first love, friendship and messy choices ahead of its September 25 premiere.
body:
• The first full trailer for Don't Be Shy, produced by Alia Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt under Eternal Sunshine Productions, released on September 11, 2026.
  • Written and directed by Sreeti Mukerji, the coming-of-age romantic comedy introduces four newcomers — Aarushi Bajaj, Piyush Khati, Bianca Arora and Ansh Duggal — in the lead roles.
  • The film follows Shyamili "Shy" Das, a 20-year-old whose carefully planned life unravels, pulling her between her feelings for Mayank, her estranged childhood friend Dhruv, and the arrival of Tara.
  • It streams exclusively on Prime Video from September 25, 2026, in Hindi with English subtitles, available across India and more than 240 countries and territories.

The first full trailer for Don't Be Shy, the coming-of-age romantic comedy produced by Alia Bhatt and her sister Shaheen Bhatt, arrived on September 11, giving audiences their first substantial look at the film's story and its four debutant leads. The two-minute-plus trailer traces the fallout of Shyamili "Shy" Das, a 20-year-old who believes she has her life mapped out, as her plans collapse into a tangle of first love, old friendships and messy choices.

Written and directed by Sreeti Mukerji, the film marks a notable casting gamble: instead of established names, its entire romantic-comedy quartet is played by newcomers. Aarushi Bajaj stars as Shy, with Piyush Khati as Mayank, Ansh Duggal as Dhruv and Bianca Arora as Tara. The trailer lays out the central triangle — Shy trying to regain control of her life while navigating feelings for Mayank and her estranged childhood friend Dhruv — with Tara's arrival adding another layer of complication. Kunaal Roy Kapur, Anurag Basu, Neha Dhupia and Anju Alva Naik round out the supporting cast in pivotal roles.

Context: Eternal Sunshine's growing production slate

Don't Be Shy is produced by Alia and Shaheen Bhatt through their banner, Eternal Sunshine Productions, and co-produced by Grishma Shah and Vikesh Bhutani under Chalkboard Entertainment. The film is a Prime Video original, set to stream in Hindi with English subtitles from September 25, 2026, across India and more than 240 countries and territories worldwide.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=7wuO-q6G0qw

The sisters have steadily built a production track record backing Darlings, Jigra and Poacher, and Don't Be Shy continues their pattern of supporting projects with a distinctive creative voice. Director Sreeti Mukerji previously worked on the direction teams of Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani, Ae Dil Hai Mushkil and Brahmastra Part One: Shiva before making her feature debut here. The trailer launch in Mumbai was accompanied by a promotional event, the "Don't Be Shy Fest," where Alia Bhatt appeared alongside the young cast. Two songs from the film — "Tere Sang," performed by Armaan Malik and Yaashasvii Ddasane, and the peppy track "Jhoomo" — have already been released.

"What excites us most is this brilliant young cast; their energy, vulnerability, and chemistry are magnetic, and they bring such life and honesty to these characters. We can't wait for audiences in India and around the world to meet Shy and get swept into her wonderful, chaotic world."

— Alia Bhatt, speaking about the film's ensemble cast

Impact: a bet on new faces in a star-driven market

Hindi cinema's recent box-office history has been dominated by star vehicles, making Don't Be Shy a genuine outlier: a mainstream-platform release whose principal cast consists entirely of unknown names. The approach puts the weight of the film squarely on its writing and direction, with the trailer's reception suggesting Prime Video is positioning it as a youthful, music-driven streaming title rather than a theatrical-style event film.

The trailer's focus on Shy's attempt to "put things back in order" after her life veers off track, as described in the coverage, sets up a familiar but durable coming-of-age premise — friendship, heartbreak and self-discovery in the early adult years. For Mukerji, whose assistant-direction credits include some of the biggest Hindi films of the last decade, the film is her first outing as the sole creative lead.

"It captures something so honest about being young — the friendships that shape you, the first loves that change you, the heartbreaks that stay with you, and the process of gradually figuring out who you are."

— Alia Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt, in a joint statement on the film

Diaspora angle

The September 25 premiere on Prime Video, day-and-date across more than 240 countries and territories with English subtitles, means the film lands in diaspora living rooms — from the Bay Area to London to Toronto — at the same time as in India. For NRI families, the college-set story of first love and growing pains travels without needing much cultural translation.

What's next

With the trailer out and the promotional push underway, all attention turns to the September 25 streaming debut. Early reception of the trailer, the music tracks and the young ensemble's launch will determine whether Don't Be Shy becomes Eternal Sunshine's breakout production success or a cautionary note on the limits of the newcomers-first model.
